clues.text: With only his armor-bearer beside him, Saul's son climbed a cliff on hands and feet to attack a Philistine outpost.
Not knowing his father Saul's oath against eating, he dipped his staff into honeycomb in the forest, and his eyes brightened.
Soon after David killed the Philistine giant, this man gave David his own robe, tunic, sword, bow and belt.
In a field near the stone Ezel, he shot an arrow beyond a boy as a secret signal for David to flee.
At the New Moon meal, King Saul hurled a spear at his own son for defending David.
The Philistines killed him along with his brothers Abinadab and Malchishua in the battle on Mount Gilboa.
In his lament, David called this friend his brother and said his love surpassed the love of women.
